I will keep all 15.0 mu in cotton this year. I have farmed this crop for decades, so I do not start from zero. I start from what worked for me in recent years and adjust a little for cost and water. With well irrigation, I can push yield more steadily, so I will not save money by cutting fertilizer too hard. Cotton here needs a stable base of nitrogen, but I do not like putting all of it up front because too much early nitrogen gives me tall plants and more useless vegetative growth. I will put most phosphorus as base fertilizer because it helps rooting early, and I will keep potassium solid because cotton pulls a lot of it once bolls start setting. On 15 mu, I can still manage carefully with family labor, but I also think about efficiency, so I will keep the field ploughed and leveled well, use hybrid seed, irrigate about 4 times if rainfall is normal, and plan on around 5 pesticide rounds for aphids, mirids, bollworm, mites, and late-season disease pressure. If the season is normal, I will aim for about 350 kg per mu of seed cotton. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and protect the yield than save a small amount and lose production.
